name: Computer Science, B.S.
college: College of Engineering and Computing Sciences
source_notes: Curriculum blocks scraped from NYIT public catalog 2026-2027. Individual course prerequisites cross-referenced with the official 2022 Semester Map PDF (site.nyit.edu/files/advising/semester_maps_2022/ADV_DegreeMap_COECS_ComputerScienceBS_2022.pdf). Where the 2026-2027 catalog uses course codes that did not appear in the 2022 map, prereqs default to empty and are marked TODO for follow-up.

requirement_blocks.name: General Education — Seminars (3 of 4 areas)
requirement_blocks.notes: Students must take three seminar courses from three different areas of study.

requirement_blocks.name: Engineering Technology
requirement_blocks.notes: ETCS 105 may be waived for transfer students with sophomore+ status.

requirement_blocks.name: Core Computer Science
requirement_blocks.notes: AI concentration substitutes CSCI 435 for CSCI 270.

requirement_blocks.name: Electives
requirement_blocks.notes: 9 Math/Science Elective + 3 General Elective + 3 Liberal Arts Elective. All electives must be approved by the department.

concentrations.name: Artificial Intelligence
concentrations.description: Choose four courses from the AI concentration list. Substitute CSCI 435 for CSCI 270 in the core.

concentrations.name: Big Data Management and Analytics
concentrations.description: Choose four courses from the Big Data concentration list.

concentrations.name: Network Security
concentrations.description: Choose four courses from the Network Security concentration list.

concentrations.name: General Option
concentrations.description: Choose four CSCI/ITEC 300- or 400-level courses (excluding CSCI 316 and CSCI 317).

courses.title: Computer Programming I
courses.description: Introduction to computer programming and problem solving using a high-level language.

courses.title: Digital Logic Design Fundamentals
courses.description: Fundamentals of digital logic design including Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits.

courses.title: Computer Organization and Architecture
courses.description: Computer organization at the assembly language level, memory hierarchy, and processor architecture.

courses.title: Computer Programming II
courses.description: Object-oriented programming, data abstraction, and program design.

courses.title: Elements of Discrete Structures
courses.description: Logic, sets, functions, relations, proof techniques, counting, algorithmic analysis, graph theory, and trees.

courses.title: Data Structures
courses.description: Classic data structures — stacks, queues, linked lists, binary trees — with sorting, searching, and computational analysis.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics for Computer Science
courses.description: Probability, discrete and continuous distributions, statistical inference, and applications in computer science.

courses.title: Database Management
courses.description: Relational database design, SQL, normalization, transactions, and database administration.

courses.title: Theory of Computation
courses.description: Formal languages, automata theory, computability, and complexity.

courses.title: Programming Language Concepts
courses.description: Comparative study of programming language paradigms — imperative, functional, object-oriented, logic.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Process management, memory management, file systems, concurrency, and OS design.

courses.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: Algorithm design techniques, complexity analysis, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, NP-completeness.

courses.title: Computer Networks
courses.description: Network architectures, OSI/TCP-IP models, routing, transport protocols, and network security fundamentals.

courses.title: Introduction to Software Engineering
courses.description: Software development lifecycle, requirements, design patterns, testing, agile methodologies.

courses.title: Senior Project I
courses.description: First half of the senior capstone: project proposal, requirements, and design.

courses.title: Senior Project II
courses.description: Second half of the senior capstone: implementation, testing, and presentation.

courses.title: Programming for Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Programming techniques for AI systems — search, knowledge representation, symbolic reasoning.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence I
courses.description: Search algorithms, knowledge representation, logic, planning, and introductory machine learning.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence II
courses.description: Advanced AI topics — probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian networks, reinforcement learning, and applications.

courses.title: Optimization Methods
courses.description: Linear and nonlinear optimization techniques for AI and operations research.

courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: Supervised and unsupervised learning, neural networks, model evaluation, and practical ML pipelines.

courses.title: Probability and Statistical Methods
courses.description: AI-concentration substitute for CSCI 270; emphasizes ML-relevant statistical methods.

courses.title: Special Topics I
courses.description: Rotating advanced topic in computer science.

courses.title: Special Topics II
courses.description: Rotating advanced topic in computer science.

courses.title: Database Interfaces and Programming
courses.description: Advanced database programming, ORM, stored procedures, and application interfaces.

courses.title: Distributed Database Systems
courses.description: Distributed databases, replication, partitioning, and consistency models.

courses.title: Introduction to Data Mining
courses.description: Data mining concepts, algorithms, and applications — classification, clustering, association rules.

courses.title: Information Retrieval
courses.description: Text indexing, search engines, ranking algorithms, and web information retrieval.

courses.title: Big Data Management and Analytics
courses.description: Big data ecosystems — Hadoop, Spark, NoSQL — and large-scale analytics.

courses.title: Introduction to Network and Internet Security
courses.description: Foundations of network and Internet security — threats, defenses, cryptographic basics.

courses.title: Principles of Information Security
courses.description: Information security principles, risk management, and security policy.

courses.title: CISCO Academy Level I
courses.description: Cisco Networking Academy curriculum — routing, switching, and network fundamentals.

courses.title: Information System Security Engineering and Administration
courses.description: Design, implementation, and administration of secure information systems.

courses.title: Advanced Network and Internet Security
courses.description: Advanced topics in network security — intrusion detection, secure protocols, forensics.

courses.title: Operating System Security
courses.description: OS security models, access control, secure kernels, and hardening.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Limits, continuity, differentiation, and applications.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Integration techniques, sequences, series, and applications.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, eigenvalues.

courses.title: Writing I: Foundations of College Composition
courses.description: Foundations of college-level writing and composition.

courses.title: Writing II: Foundations of Research Writing
courses.description: Research writing, source evaluation, and academic argumentation.

courses.title: Communication for Technical Professions
courses.description: Technical communication for engineering and computing professions.

courses.title: Making Sense of a Data-Oriented Society
courses.description: Data literacy for informed citizenship — statistics, data visualization, and critical thinking.

courses.title: Technology and Global Issues
courses.description: Technology's role in global society, ethics, and policy.

courses.title: General Physics I
courses.description: Classical mechanics — kinematics, dynamics, energy, momentum.

courses.title: General Physics II
courses.description: Electricity, magnetism, waves, and optics.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: Atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, and thermodynamics.

courses.title: General Biology I
courses.description: Cell biology, genetics, and evolution.

courses.title: Career Discovery
courses.description: Career exploration in engineering and computing.

courses.title: Computer, Internet, and Society
courses.description: Social, ethical, and legal issues in computing.
